claims.text: Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Prolonged conventional high-temperature sintering of ZrB2 typically produces larger grains.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 routinely has relatively high residual porosity and microstructural defects.
Residual pores in conventional ZrB2 act as crack-nucleation sites under corrosive liquid-plating conditions.
SPS using ultrafine, high-purity ZrB2 powder can lower the sintering temperature to approximately 1700–1800 °C.
A liquid-precursor route can produce high-purity, submicron ZrB2 powder suitable for the proposed SPS process.
Mechanical activation can produce high-purity, submicron ZrB2 powder suitable for the proposed SPS process.
The proposed SPS preparation uses 1700–1800 °C, rapid heating, a dwell of minutes, approximately 50–60 MPa uniaxial pressure, and an inert atmosphere.
The proposed SPS process will achieve near-full densification in single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed SPS process will retain an ultrafine ZrB2 grain size.
Rapid SPS heating and short processing suppress grain growth.
SPS suppresses oxygen uptake in ZrB2 during preparation.
SPS will produce near-zero residual porosity in the ZrB2.
Reducing residual porosity and other defects minimizes microcrack formation during corrosive plating.
A refined, low-porosity microstructure improves resistance to chemical and mechanical degradation during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have significantly lower porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will maintain greater structural integrity, form fewer holes, and fail later during long-duration plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Powder-quality variability may affect reproducibility of the proposed SPS process.
